Project CMSY++ Results under Fishing Scenarios

Source: R/cmsy_tools.R
cmsy_forecast.Rd

This function projects each stock forward from the results of cmsy_run() under fishing mortality scenarios (by default 0.5, 0.6, 0.8 and 0.95 Fmsy, as in Froese et al. 2018, and the last-year fishing mortality) or constant catches, and draws the projected B/Bmsy and catch.

Usage

cmsy_forecast(
  result,
  stocks = NULL,
  years = 10,
  f = c(0.5, 0.6, 0.8, 0.95),
  status_quo = TRUE,
  catch = NULL,
  sigma = 0.1,
  seed = NULL,
  plot = TRUE,
  table = TRUE,
  lang = NULL,
  annotations = getOption("faofishingreport.cmsy_annotations", FALSE),
  pptx = getOption("faofishingreport.pptx", FALSE),
  silent = fao_setting("silent")
)

Arguments

result

The result of cmsy_run().

stocks

Optional stocks to project: Stock identifiers or species, by English or Chinese FAO name, scientific name or FAO 3-alpha code. Default is NULL, all stocks that ran.

years

Number of years to project. Default is 10.

f

Fishing mortality scenarios as multiples of Fmsy. Default is c(0.5, 0.6, 0.8, 0.95).

status_quo

A logical value. If TRUE (default), the last-year fishing mortality is also projected.

catch

Optional constant catches to project, in tonnes per year (e.g. the last-year catch).

sigma

Standard deviation of the lognormal process error. Default is 0.1.

seed

Optional random seed.

plot, table

Whether charts (figures/png/cmsy/<stock>/forecast.png and figures/png/cmsy/summary/forecast_share.png) and the table (tables/cmsy/) are saved. Default is TRUE.

lang

The language of the chart text and names: "en" (English), "zh" (Chinese) or "both" (Chinese and English). Default is NULL, which uses the language set with fao_settings() ("en" unless changed).

annotations

The text added to the axis titles and labels: FALSE (default) none, TRUE all, or any of "title", "subtitle", "caption", "legend" and "labels" (text inside the chart). The default can be changed for the session with options(faofishingreport.cmsy_annotations = TRUE).

pptx

A logical value. If TRUE, the charts are also saved as editable PowerPoint files in figures/pptx/cmsy/<stock>/ and figures/pptx/cmsy/summary/. Default is FALSE, which can be changed for all functions with fao_settings(pptx = TRUE).

silent

A logical value. If FALSE (default), a progress bar shows how many stocks have been projected. If TRUE, nothing is printed. The default can be changed for the session with fao_settings(silent = TRUE).

Value

Invisibly, a list with projection (by stock, scenario and year: median B/Bmsy, F/Fmsy and catch with 95% limits, and the probability that B is at least Bmsy) and share (by scenario and year: share of stocks at or above Bmsy, with 95% limits).

Details

CMSY++16.R has no projection, so it is done here with the CMSY++ model itself: the Schaefer surplus-production model in which productivity declines linearly below B/k = 0.25 (CMSY++16.R and Froese et al. 2023), started from the posterior draws of r, k and last-year B/k of the run (which come from the same MCMC iterations), with lognormal process error (sigma, 0.1 by default as sigmaR in CMSY++). In the F scenarios Fmsy is reduced linearly below half of Bmsy, as in the management results of CMSY++. Catch is F times biomass, as CMSY++ defines F.

References

Froese, R., Winker, H., Coro, G., Demirel, N., Tsikliras, A.C., Dimarchopoulou, D., Scarcella, G., Quaas, M. and Matz-Lueck, N. (2018). Status and rebuilding of European fisheries. Marine Policy 93: 159-170. doi:10.1016/j.marpol.2018.04.018

Froese, R., Winker, H., Coro, G., Palomares, M.L.D., Tsikliras, A.C., Dimarchopoulou, D., Touloumis, K., Demirel, N., Vianna, G.M.S., Scarcella, G., Schijns, R., Liang, C. and Pauly, D. (2023). New developments in the analysis of catch time series as the basis for fish stock assessments: the CMSY++ method. Acta Ichthyologica et Piscatoria 53: 173-189. doi:10.3897/aiep.53.105910

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# result <- cmsy_run(...), see cmsy_run()

# Default scenarios: 0.5, 0.6, 0.8 and 0.95 Fmsy, and the last-year fishing mortality
projection <- cmsy_forecast(result, seed = 1)

# Twenty years, two F scenarios and a constant catch of 50,000 t, in Chinese
projection <- cmsy_forecast(result, years = 20, f = c(0.8, 1), catch = 50000, seed = 1, lang = "zh")
last <- projection$projection[projection$projection$Year == max(projection$projection$Year), ]
last[, c("Stock", "scenario_label", "B_Bmsy", "B_Bmsy_lcl", "B_Bmsy_ucl", "p_above_bmsy")]

# Share of the stocks at or above Bmsy (when several stocks were run)
projection$share
} # }
